newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler sees room for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler sees room for rate cut.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Tuesday that he saw some room for interest rate cuts in Germany and that further action by the end of the year could not be ruled out.
"It could be the case that speculation of a further interest rate cut could be built up (in markets)," Zeitler said.

Zeitler, who is president of the regional state central bank of Bavaria, also said he believed German M3 money supply growth, a key economic indicator, would near the German central bank's 1996 target growth range of four to seven percent.

In addition, Zeitler said he believed Germany would fulfil criteria laid out in the Maastricht Treaty for membership in the single European currency but that the treaty also allows for conceivable delay.
Zeitler made the comments to journalists following a speech to a local group.
